name: Mercury230 Client
info: Reads every current value of an Incotex Меркурий 230 electricity meter over TCP (a gateway on its RS-485 port), via the shared Mercury230Client class registered on functionGlobalContext in settings.js: serial number, firmware, status word, clock, instant values (P, Q, S, U, I, cos φ, angles, frequency) and the energy registers A+, A-, R+, R- for the tariff sum and tariffs 1-4 plus A+ per phase, raw and named after the protocol (Psum, U1, I1, energy.sum.Aplus...). Giving them their meaning is left to the flow's collect-device-state. Send any message in to trigger a read; a new message comes out with `msg.payload` set to the result. On failure nothing goes out and node.error() is called. ADDRESS is the meter's network address; PASSWORD the level-1 channel password (6 digits).

name: EK270 IEC61107 Client
info: Reads an EK270 gas volume corrector over TCP (e.g. via a МТЭК-2/3 GPRS gateway), using the IEC 61107-2001 programming-mode handshake, via the shared Ek270Iec61107Client class registered on functionGlobalContext in settings.js: the volume counters, flow rates, pressure, temperature, correction factor, identity, statuses (lists of active message numbers) and remaining battery life, raw and keyed by their IEC 61107 address (2:302, 7:310, 1:100...). Giving them their meaning is left to the flow's collect-device-state. Every value comes from a reply whose BCC is valid and whose echoed address matches the request, so another master's frames on the shared line are skipped; a poll that cannot get every value fails instead of storing shifted values. Send any message in to trigger a read; the result comes out in `msg.payload`. On failure nothing goes out and node.error() is called.

name: VKT7 Client
info:
Reads every current value of a Teplokom VKT-7 heat calculator over TCP (e.g. a Wiznet modem on its serial port), via the shared Vkt7Client class registered on functionGlobalContext in settings.js: service info, the units the device reports, current values and current totals of heat inputs input1/input2 and the device-wide elements, raw, named after the protocol's element table (t1, t2, P1, G1, V1, M1, Qo, VNR, VOS, NS...). Choosing the supply/return elements is left to the flow's collect-device-state. Send any message in to trigger a read; the same message comes out with `msg.payload` set to the result (null for elements outside the measurement scheme or with bad quality, deviceTime/timestamp as epoch ms). On failure nothing goes out and node.error() is called. ADDRESS is the calculator's network number (the built-in RS-485 adapter does not answer 0); WAKE_UP_BYTES is the count of 0xFF bytes before each request (2 for RS-232, 0 is fine for RS-485).

Through a БАРС-02 GPRS unit, which connects to us instead of waiting for a connection: set BARS02_ID to the identifier the unit sends (its CBN, e.g. Строителей_53); HOST and PORT are then unused. The unit connects to the gateway listening on BARS02_LISTEN_PORT (published by docker-compose; the office router forwards a public port to it; started at deploy), which reads one meter per unit at a time. BARS02_LINE is the meter line the unit sets before each read: rs232 | rs232-powered | rs485, baud rate, 8N1 / 8E1 / 8O1 / 8N2 (the old dispatch system's port settings), or none for old-firmware units (3.0.1), which keep the line their configuration sets. Over GPRS a request takes 4-5 s and a whole read 30-90 s, so the read allows 15 s per request and at least 240 s in all. See .docs/bars02/bars02-notes.md.

name: KM5 Client
info:
Reads every current value of a TBN KM-5 heat meter over TCP (e.g. a Maestro modem on its RS-485 port), via the shared Km5Client class registered on functionGlobalContext in settings.js: firmware and type, status bytes, current values (commands 123 and 94) and totals with the clock (command 95), raw in the device's units and named after the protocol (GM1, GV1, t1, P1, W, M1, V1, Q, Tr...). Choosing the supply/return values is left to the flow's collect-device-state. Send any message in to trigger a read; the same message comes out with `msg.payload` set to the result (deviceTime/timestamp as epoch ms). On failure nothing goes out and node.error() is called. ADDRESS is the meter's network number, which is its factory number (e.g. 418200).

Through a БАРС-02 GPRS unit, which connects to us instead of waiting for a connection: set BARS02_ID to the identifier the unit sends (its CBN, e.g. Строителей_15); HOST and PORT are then unused. The unit connects to the gateway listening on BARS02_LISTEN_PORT (published by docker-compose; the office router forwards a public port to it; started at deploy), which reads one meter per unit at a time. BARS02_LINE is the meter line the unit sets before each read: rs232 | rs232-powered | rs485, baud rate, 8N1 / 8E1 / 8O1 / 8N2 (default rs485 9600 8N1, the old dispatch system's port settings), or none for old-firmware units (3.0.1), which keep the line their configuration sets. Over GPRS a request takes 4-5 s, so the read allows 15 s per request and at least 240 s in all; a garbled reply is repeated after 2 s of silence. The РМ-5 speaks the same protocol (ADDRESS = its factory number, RS-485 9600 8N1); replies that lost their first 4 bytes (the network number) are accepted when they are valid with it put back. See .docs/bars02/bars02-notes.md.

name: TV7 Client
info:
Reads every current value of a Termotronic TV7 heat calculator over TCP (e.g. a Wiznet modem on its RS-232/RS-485 port), via the shared Tv7Client class registered on functionGlobalContext in settings.js: device info, instant values and totals for heat inputs input1/input2 and their pipes pipe1-pipe3, raw in SI units (GJ, MPa, m3, t) and named after the protocol tables (t, P, Go, Gm, F, V, M, Ftv, Qtv, VNR, VOS, NS...). Choosing the supply/return pipe and converting units is left to the flow's collect-device-state. Send any message in to trigger a read; the same message comes out with `msg.payload` set to the result (deviceTime/timestamp as epoch ms). On failure nothing goes out and node.error() is called. ADDRESS is the Modbus network address (1 by default); SERIAL_NUMBER, when set, is checked against the device's factory number.

Through a БАРС-02 GPRS unit, which connects to us instead of waiting for a connection: set BARS02_ID to the identifier the unit sends (its CBN, e.g. Строителей_15); HOST and PORT are then unused. The unit connects to the gateway listening on BARS02_LISTEN_PORT (published by docker-compose; the office router forwards a public port to it; started at deploy), which reads one meter per unit at a time. BARS02_LINE is the meter line the unit sets before each read: rs232 | rs232-powered | rs485, baud rate, 8N1 / 8E1 / 8O1 / 8N2 (default rs232-powered 9600 8N1, the old dispatch system's port settings), or none for old-firmware units (3.0.1), which keep the line their configuration sets. Over GPRS a request takes 4-5 s, so the read allows 15 s per request and at least 240 s in all; a garbled reply is repeated after 2 s of silence. Set SERIAL_NUMBER to the meter's factory number or empty (the default belongs to the example meter 19072584). Firmware 1.00 (the ТВ7 behind the БАРС-02 units, 2026-10-26) refuses the totals in one request; the client reads them in parts and leaves the device-wide block 3513-3532 (operating times, events, Qсум) null. See .docs/bars02/bars02-notes.md.
